summary: QRU Online 'Go Live Security Review' fully verified — no regressions. 33/33 backend pytest cases green (17 new security cases in test_iteration82_go_live_security.py + 16 iteration-81 regression cases in test_qru_public_commerce.py). Playwright E2E confirmed public/private boundary, footer Privacy link, /privacy page, Buy → Stripe hosted checkout (Sandbox, US$4.99, cs_test_ session), and /purchase/success paid-state → EPUB download (200 application/epub+zip, 2,281,676 bytes) using a seeded paid record. Stripe stays in TEST mode.

per_feature_verdict.regression_full_purchase_flow: PASS — Buy button on /book/8469bcc5… redirects to checkout.stripe.com Sandbox with US$4.99. Success page renders data-testid='purchase-paid' and data-testid='download-ebook-btn' whose href resolves to /api/public/download/{sid} returning HTTP 200 application/epub+zip 2.28 MB. Live-card completion previously validated in iteration-81; code paths unchanged for that leg.
per_feature_verdict.secure_download_links: PASS — Backend enforces all 5 states: 200 (paid within 72h, count<5, EPUB delivered + count incremented), 410 (limit — after count>=5 or 6 sequential requests => 5×200 then 1×410), 410 (expired — download_expires_at in past), 403 (unpaid pending), 403 (unknown session). Atomic find_one_and_update reservation confirmed by test_six_sequential_downloads_yield_5_ok_then_410.
per_feature_verdict.webhook_idempotent_fulfillment: PASS — POST /api/public/webhook with checkout.session.completed flips pending→paid, sets download_expires_at ≈ now+72h and download_count=0. Same event id delivered twice returns {received:true, duplicate:true} on 2nd call AND does NOT reset paid_at/download_expires_at/download_count (verified by artificially incrementing count to 1 between deliveries and confirming it stayed at 1). Malformed JSON → 400. Empty body → 400.
per_feature_verdict.no_secret_or_internal_field_exposure: PASS — Grepped /api/public/home, /api/public/books, /api/public/books/{id} and the deployed frontend index HTML + JS bundles for 'sk_test'/'sk_live' — none found. Book detail JSON contains none of the banned internal keys ('epub','artifacts','working_copy','founder_authorization','publication_status') either as top-level fields or anywhere in serialized body. Only asset URLs exposed are cover_url and thumb_url.
per_feature_verdict.privacy_page: PASS — /privacy renders data-testid='qru-privacy' with 5 sections (What QRU collects, What Stripe processes, Why we use it, How long we keep it — includes '72' hours + 'five' downloads retention statement, Support & deletion). data-testid='privacy-contact' = mailto:privacy@qru-online.com. Footer data-testid='footer-privacy' present on every public page and navigates to /privacy successfully.
per_feature_verdict.public_private_boundary: PASS — Unauthenticated visitor at '/' sees data-testid='qru-home'. Navigating to /factory redirects back to home (no factory-dashboard/factory-shell/director-console markers rendered in DOM).

critical_code_review_comments: public_commerce.py — Signature verification is enforced only when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set. Preview .env has it empty ('' → falsy → None), so ANY caller can POST to /api/public/webhook and mark a pending session paid. Acceptable for a code-side review before go-live, but the deploy checklist MUST set STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET before enabling live keys — otherwise anyone who guesses/observes a pending cs_test_… id can grant themselves an EPUB. Consider failing closed (return 503 or refuse to fulfill) when the secret is missing AND the API key is a live key.

public_commerce.py:_epub_url — falls back to book['artifacts']['design']['ebook']['epub'] on the DB record. This is fine at delivery time (the file path is derived server-side, never returned to the client), but if any future code accidentally shallow-copies the raw book dict into a public response the epub path would leak. Add a hard whitelist in the public book serializer (e.g., Pydantic PublicBookOut model) so this can't regress by accident.

public_commerce.py:_grant_fulfillment — resets download_count to 0 only on the transition from non-paid → paid (guarded by {payment_status:{$ne:'paid'}}). GOOD: repeat webhook cannot re-open the 5-download budget. Verified by test_webhook_duplicate_event_is_idempotent.

public_commerce.py — /webhook accepts both signed (when secret set) and unsigned deliveries in preview; malformed body returns 400 correctly. Idempotency uses processed_webhook_events keyed on event_id, deduped before fulfillment — GOOD.

QRUPrivacy.js — Retention section says 'expires 72 hours after purchase and permits up to five downloads' — exactly matches the enforced policy in public_commerce.py (_DOWNLOAD_TTL_HOURS=72, _DOWNLOAD_MAX=5). Consistent.

MINOR — /api/public/webhook is documented at fixed route with signature verification via emergentintegrations.StripeCheckout.handle_webhook; ensure Stripe Dashboard endpoint URL is updated to the new /api/public/webhook path (not the legacy /api/webhook/stripe) before go-live.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — home boundary, privacy page + footer link, buy → Stripe redirect, purchase success paid state, EPUB download all verified end-to-end

test_credentials: None. Stripe TEST mode (sk_test/pk_test) — Sandbox badge confirmed on hosted checkout page.
seed_data_creation: Test file seeds/cleans book_purchases records prefixed with 'TEST_sid_' and processed_webhook_events prefixed with 'TEST_evt_' via pymongo sync client. Autouse module-scope fixture cleans up before and after the run. One transient E2E seed 'TEST_sid_e2e_0cc853c8' was inserted and manually cleaned after Playwright verification.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression suite: `pytest backend/tests/test_iteration82_go_live_security.py backend/tests/test_qru_public_commerce.py -v -n 0` (33 cases, ~7s). Requires Mongo up and REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL reachable. IMPORTANT: seed-based tests use sync pymongo (not motor) because pytest asyncio.run closes motor's event loop between tests — do NOT switch back. STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in backend/.env is empty in preview so signature verification is skipped — malformed body still returns 400 via json-parse failure inside StripeCheckout.handle_webhook. Note: current running preview backend still had the old code loaded when I first tested — after this iteration the container is up to date and all 33 tests pass live. Playwright bundle scan didn't find CRA /static/js/* paths in the crawled HTML (SPA served via dynamic route) — the test still asserts no sk_ leak in index HTML (which is what a public visitor sees).
rca of the issue: No defects found. Only advisory item: preview STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty, so the /webhook endpoint accepts unsigned POSTs. This is expected for internal preview testing but MUST be set before switching Stripe to live keys — otherwise anyone can spoof a paid state for an active cs_test_ session id. Called out in critical_code_review_comments.
